title: Determining Hydrogen Peroxide Concentration by Redox Titration
description: A guided-inquiry redox titration investigation with a 15-minute practice, one-minute report, teacher-approved redesign, permanganate standardization, two assigned hydrogen peroxide samples, density-based percent-by-mass calculations, and source-labeled class comparison.
audience: Chemistry students preparing for or reflecting on a wet-lab permanganate titration
learningGoals: Standardize KMnO4 solution against acidified 0.100 M Fe2+ using fresh burette readings and the 1:5 permanganate-to-iron stoichiometry.
Distinguish a colorless pre-endpoint mixture, a persistent faint-pink endpoint, and a dark red-purple overshoot that invalidates a quantitative trial.
Determine percent H2O2 by mass for two assigned samples using standardized KMnO4, 2:5 permanganate-to-peroxide stoichiometry, and a configured density of 1.00 g/mL.
Evaluate replicate precision, retain class-data provenance, and justify procedural improvements and outlier decisions.
safetyNotes: Review the SDS or instructor-provided safety information for KMnO4 solution, H2O2 samples, 6 M H2SO4, and Fe(NH4)2(SO4)2·6H2O before beginning.
Wear splash-proof goggles and a lab apron; gloves are strongly recommended, and proper ventilation is required.
Never combine solid KMnO4 with H2SO4. This investigation uses KMnO4 solution only; the solid-acid combination can be explosive.
Treat sulfuric acid and permanganate as capable of causing skin burns and eye damage. Immediately wash a skin spill with copious water and notify the instructor.
Use only the teacher-configured local/state/instructor waste procedure. This activity does not invent or assume a drain-disposal route.
